blocks.content: Dynamic provisioning is the modern, automated way Persistent Volumes actually get created, on demand, the moment a PVC needs one, instead of an administrator creating them ahead of time.

Before dynamic provisioning, an administrator had to manually create a pool of PVs ahead of time, anticipating what storage might be needed, and PVCs could only bind to whatever happened to already exist.

blocks.alt: Storage created ahead of time, based on anticipated future need

blocks.content: 2. The Modern Way: Created Automatically, on Demand
blocks.text: 2. The Modern Way: Created Automatically, on Demand

blocks.content: With dynamic provisioning, creating a PVC is enough on its own, if no existing PV matches, one is created automatically, right then, specifically to satisfy that claim, no administrator has to be involved at all.

blocks.alt: A PV appears automatically, the moment a PVC actually needs one

blocks.content: This is exactly the StorageClass mechanism covered in the previous topic in action, a PVC references a StorageClass, and that class's provisioner is triggered to create a brand new, matching PV, automatically, satisfying the claim without any pre-existing PV needing to be there first.

blocks.alt: A PVC and a StorageClass together, triggering automatic PV creation

blocks.content: 4. The Standard Default on Modern Cloud Clusters
blocks.text: 4. The Standard Default on Modern Cloud Clusters

blocks.content: Nearly every managed Kubernetes offering (EKS, GKE, AKS, and similar) ships with dynamic provisioning enabled and a sensible default StorageClass already configured, static provisioning is now the exception, reserved for specific, unusual storage requirements.

blocks.alt: The default experience on virtually every modern managed cluster

blocks.content: It is worth remembering that dynamic provisioning does not change the fundamental PV/PVC binding relationship covered earlier in this module, it only changes how the PV comes into existence in the first place, the actual binding mechanics work identically either way.

blocks.alt: The same PV/PVC relationship, regardless of how the PV was actually created

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Dynamic provisioning creates a matching PV automatically the moment a PVC needs one, using the StorageClass mechanism, no administrator pre-creation required.
It is the modern default on virtually every cloud-managed cluster, static provisioning by hand is now the exception rather than the norm.
